transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Security PM); Dr. Aaron Blake, Sofia Martinez, Omar Khalid, Priya Nair (Stratos)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through security posture and how 'no-train' commitments are supported across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Stratos asked about PHI pathways, audit log fidelity, and EU-only residency. Action items agreed at end.

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. I'm Maya with Redwood, I'll kick us off. We have Ravi our SE and Lena from Security. Could we quick intro from Stratos?
[00:08] Dr. Aaron Blake: Yeah hi, Aaron Blake. I look after data governance. Our main ask today is we need firm assurances that customer data, especially PHI, will not be used to train any models unless specifically contracted.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: Hi Sofia, ML lead. We're trying to evaluate private deployment but want to understand options and tradeoffs.
[00:24] Omar Khalid: Omar, security architect — I'm focused on keys, HSM, audit trails, and SSO.
[00:29] Priya Nair: Priya from procurement, just listening for the legal bits.
[00:33] Ravi Patel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — cover our commitments around data usage, then KMS/HSM options, audit logs, residency, and RBAC/SSO. We'll leave time for bench discussion.
[00:44] Dr. Aaron Blake: Cool. So first, 'no-train' — we've seen vendors say 'we don't train on customer data' but then it's fuzzy. Do you have hard guarantees?
[00:54] Lena Ortiz: I can take that. Our standard is that hosted API customers can opt into a tenant that opts out of data training; for enterprise we support a contractual 'no training' clause plus an operational mode where logs used for model improvement are disabled. For Private and Dedicated — by design there is no training on your data unless you explicitly engage us for that work.
[01:12] Dr. Aaron Blake: When you say "disabled" — is that switch at the tenant level? Is there any downstream telemetry that could be used?
[01:20] Ravi Patel: The telemetry that goes to our platform for observability is tokenized metrics and per-route latency/cost aggregates. We don't persist full prompts in the hosted no-train configuration. However, with hosted customers we also offer an enterprise private control plane where telemetry can be routed to the customer's observability stack — so the raw prompts never leave their VPC.
[01:40] Sofia Martinez: Are there logs retained anywhere for debugging? We sometimes need traces to troubleshoot prompts.
[01:46] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we retain request logs but retention is configurable. For strict PHI flows we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments plus ephemeral prompt retention — by default we support 7, 30, 90 day retention windows or a zero-retention policy where logs are not persisted beyond immediate ephemeral processing.
[02:05] Omar Khalid: How is "ephemeral" implemented? Does the KV cache or disk swap store anything?
[02:12] Ravi Patel: Good question. The runtime uses an in-memory KV cache for performance. For any checkpointing or spill to disk, we encrypt with keys you control for Private deployments (BYOK). For Hosted no-train tenants, spills are disabled and any temp files are scrubbed immediately; admissible for audit but we'll share exact technical notes.
[02:32] Dr. Aaron Blake: You mentioned BYOK — do you support HSM-backed keys or cloud KMS?
[02:37] Lena Ortiz: Both. For Private we support HSM (PKCS11) and integrations with AWS KMS, Google KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For Dedicated we can do KMS with customer-managed keys. HSM is available as an add-on and can be configured so keys never leave the HSM.
[02:52] Priya Nair: Legal will want to see the key lifecycle docs.
[02:55] Maya Chen: We'll include lifecycle and rotation docs in the packet.
[02:58] [00:03:00] Sofia Martinez: Audit logs — what events are emitted? We'll need to show data access for SOC 2.
[03:05] Ravi Patel: The logs include authentication events (SAML/SO), API request id, model id, route metadata, token counts, and a hash of the prompt if you choose hashed logging. We can optionally exclude prompt text entirely. Retention is explicit in the config.
[03:20] Dr. Aaron Blake: Hashing prompts — is that reversible? Could it be used to reconstruct?
[03:25] Lena Ortiz: Hashing is one-way. If you want to correlate between runs you can keep a local mapping; Redwood does not keep the mapping for no-train tenants.
[03:34] Omar Khalid: For compliance, we need attestations — SOC 2 Type II and something for ISO. Do you have those?
[03:39] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, and an ISO 27001 summary. We'll send certs and the controls matrix.
[03:45] Priya Nair: Is there any regional residency guarantee? We operate in EU and can't have data cross-border.
[03:51] Ravi Patel: We support EU-only deployments — either in the hosted API with EU-only tenancy, or Dedicated in EU regions, and full Private on-prem or VPC-within-EU. We'll provide network diagrams showing egress controls.
[04:03] [00:04:30] Dr. Aaron Blake: If we go Private, what's the upgrade path? Also, what about patching and security updates — who is responsible?
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: In Private mode you have a customer-managed control plane; Redwood provides signed artifacts and a patch cadence. You can choose automatic patching windows or manual apply. For Dedicated we manage infra but with restricted access and change windows defined in SLA.
[04:26] Sofia Martinez: Performance-wise if we lock to EU region and enable HSM, what's the latency / cost hit?
[04:33] Ravi Patel: HSM introduces a small latency for key operations (few ms per key op) — unaffected per-token runtime. Network egress within same region is negligible. The main cost delta is reserved capacity for Dedicated or Private infra and HSM instance costs. We'll run a bench with your sample workloads.
[04:50] [00:05:30] Omar Khalid: About SSO — we use SAML + SCIM for user lifecycle. Can we enforce RBAC roles that segregate dev/test from prod and lift-only admin keys?
[04:58] Lena Ortiz: Yes — we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is granular: roles for Viewer, Operator, Model Admin, and Key Admin. Keys for BYOK can be restricted to Key Admin role. We'll show sample role mappings.
[05:12] Maya Chen: Quick note, customers sometimes confuse "no-train" with "no-logging." They are related but separate. We can do no-train but still keep metrics for billing; we can do no-logging with ephemeral handling too.
[05:25] Dr. Aaron Blake: Right. For regulators we need explicit 'no training' clause in contract, and proof that no data was used — how do you attest to that?
[05:34] Lena Ortiz: We provide contractual language plus operational controls: tenant-level flags, disabled data collection, and audit trails showing collection toggles. For Private deployments you control the plane so attestation is by configuration and logs. For hosted we provide signed audit logs and compliance artifacts.
[05:50] [00:06:30] Sofia Martinez: If we send deidentified patient notes for benchmarking, does that count as training data if we run evals?
[05:58] Ravi Patel: If you explicitly upload data into a training pipeline then yes. For evaluation runs via the inference path, we do not use that to train models unless you opt in. We'll make sure bench runs use ephemeral-only request logging.
[06:12] Dr. Aaron Blake: We may ask for guaranteed zero retention for a 6-month pilot. Is that feasible?
[06:18] Lena Ortiz: Yes — for a pilot we can configure zero retention and place guardrails — but you should expect limited debug ability. We'll also document this in the DPA addendum.
[06:28] [00:07:00] Omar Khalid: What about third-party subprocessors? Where are model weights coming from? Any external vendor with access to raw prompts?
[06:36] Maya Chen: Model weights are maintained by Redwood and our curated open-model catalog. We do use third-party infra providers (cloud regions) but customer data in Private is kept within tenant/VPC. We'll provide subprocessor list in the contract.
[06:47] Priya Nair: Audit trail detail — can you show a sample log format?
[06:51] Ravi Patel: Yes we'll send a sample JSON schema for the audit log. It will include timestamps, actor id (SAML subject), API request id, model variant, route, token_count, hash_of_prompt (optional), and a pointer to storage location if retention enabled.
[07:06] [00:07:45] Sofia Martinez: The pointer — is that to S3? Will Redwood manage that bucket? Can we own that storage?
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: You can own it in Private deployments; for Hosted we can push logs to a customer bucket via cross-account write or push to your SIEM via secure forwarder.
[07:22] Dr. Aaron Blake: Back to keys — rotation policy. Can we mandate rotation-only via HSM and that Redwood cannot export keys?
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: Yes, HSM/BYOK ensures keys never leave the HSM. Rotation can be customer-driven or automated with rotation scripts that you own. We'll document rotation workflows.
[07:40] [00:08:30] Maya Chen: A quick practical example — for a PHI workflow you'd likely choose Private with BYOK and zero retention for prompts, and keep audit logs hashed and exported to your SIEM. That combination satisfies most auditor asks.
[07:50] Dr. Aaron Blake: Sounds right. One more: Do you provide sample attestation language for procurement to include in our MSA?
[07:57] Maya Chen: Yes, Lena will attach suggested clauses for 'no-train' and data processing addendum.
[08:02] [00:09:00] Omar Khalid: On RBAC and admin keys— can an engineer request temporary elevated access? Do you have session logs?
[08:09] Ravi Patel: We support ephemeral elevation via approval workflow if integrated to your IDP. All sessions are logged with session tokens and admin actions are auditable.
[08:19] Sofia Martinez: Regarding model variants — if Redwood automatically falls back to a smaller model for cost reasons, could that introduce differences in handling of PII?
[08:27] Lena Ortiz: Our routing policies are explicit. For any tenant with sensitive data we recommend pinning model versions and disabling automatic fallbacks. The platform can enforce a policy that prevents routing to non-EU or non-dedicated variants.
[08:40] [00:09:50] Dr. Aaron Blake: Great. We need to ensure legal gets the DPA and 'no training' clause. Priya will take that. Priya, any questions?
[08:49] Priya Nair: Just timeline — if we decide to pilot next month, what's the lead time for Private deployment?
[08:55] Ravi Patel: For Private in your VPC it's typically 2-4 weeks depending on networking approvals; Dedicated in EU reserved capacity is 4-6 weeks. We'll scope exact times after we see your network team availability.
[09:06] [00:10:20] Maya Chen: Alright, we're at about 10 minutes in — I'll move to demo scheduling and bench specifics, Ravi do you want to cover the bench plan?
[09:14] Ravi Patel: Sure — plan is: you provide a deidentified sample dataset shape, we spin an instance that mirrors your token lengths and concurrency, run a 1-hour load that simulates real traffic, and capture latency, tokens/sec, and cost. For PHI constraints we'll run with zero retention and HSM if you choose BYOK.
[09:34] Sofia Martinez: For the bench can we also capture per-route cost and token breakdown?
[09:38] Ravi Patel: Yes we'll provide token-level breakdown and estimated unit economics.
[09:42] [00:11:10] Dr. Aaron Blake: One hypothetical — if a subpoena requires logs, how would that be handled given zero retention?
[09:49] Lena Ortiz: If logs are zero retention there's nothing to produce. For audit/policy you can choose a special export flow where logs are forwarded to your long-term archive before deletion; that's usually governed by process and legal hold. We'll include that in the DPA options.
[09:59] Omar Khalid: Does Redwood have a breach notification SLA?
[10:03] Maya Chen: Yes, standard incident notification with 72-hour initial notification and a defined incident response playbook. We'll send incident response summary.
[10:12] [00:11:40] Sofia Martinez: Any concerns around model hallucination that could leak internal terms? Not a security question strictly but relevant for PHI context — are there filters?
[10:21] Ravi Patel: We support content filters and response transformations; you can also run a post-processing step in your VPC to scrub outputs before storing. Again, Private gives you full control.
[10:32] Dr. Aaron Blake: Ok, we're getting close. Could you also provide evidence of encryption at rest and in transit? That's a checklist item.
[10:38] Lena Ortiz: TLS for all in transit; at rest we encrypt with customer keys for Private, and for Hosted we use provider KMS with encryption at rest and key management options described in the docs. We'll include certs and encryption diagrams.
[10:52] [00:12:15] Maya Chen: Quick pause — any blockers to proceeding with the pilot if we provide deidentified data and sign DPA?
[10:22] Dr. Aaron Blake: None on our side, assuming contract language acceptable.
[10:27] Priya Nair: Procurement requested subcontractor list — will include that in the contract packet?
[10:32] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include the subprocessor list and SOC2 attestation.
[10:40] [00:12:55] Ravi Patel: I'll also note one operational caveat — zero retention reduces our ability to do root-cause debugging for transient infra issues. We recommend a short retention window and immediate offload to your archive if you expect to debug.
[10:52] Dr. Aaron Blake: Understood.
[11:00] [00:13:30] Sofia Martinez: On the subject of model updates — if you roll out a model update in the hosted environment could that change behavior? We need regression monitoring.
[11:09] Lena Ortiz: Yes — Redwood Optimize includes evaluation gates. For enterprise tenants you can disable automatic model updates or have a canary and A/B rollout. We can also pin a model SHA.
[11:22] Maya Chen: We're at about 35 minutes left, we'll wrap with concrete next steps. Lena, any closing notes from security?
[11:29] Lena Ortiz: I'll attach exact DPA clauses, audit log schema, HSM integration guide, and suggested RBAC mapping. Also will include sample contractual 'no-train' language — note legal teams often want tighter wording; we can iterate.
[11:41] Dr. Aaron Blake: Perfect. One last quick Q: In the hosted no-train mode, you said you don't persist prompts — is there any short-lived cache that could be subpoenaed?
[11:49] Ravi Patel: Only ephemeral memory; for hosted no-train we don't write full request payloads to durable storage. Any ephemeral artifacts are scrubbed; we'll include forensic notes.
[11:59] [00:15:00] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone. We'll review docs when you send them.
[12:03] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet and schedule the bench.
[12:07] Dr. Aaron Blake: Thanks.
